craft_playbook: Deliver the hook inside 2.5 seconds; viewers decide in under 2 on mobile.
Open with a pattern interrupt or curiosity gap; NEVER context/build-up or greetings.
Reverse structure: lead with the payoff (news, boldest number, verdict tease), explain after.
Include a concrete number in the hook when possible (price, 0-100, sales figure).
No dead air: trim silences; keep delivery slightly faster than conversational.
Bury nothing: the best moment goes first, not 15 seconds in.
One idea per beat; cut visuals every 2-3 seconds; open on motion or high-contrast frame.
End with a question that begs a comment + a loop-friendly closer (last line can feed the first).
Hook and content must match; clickbait mismatch kills retention and trust.
Front-load value beats: price/verdict by the midpoint, never last.

NEVER recycle a joke or catchphrase across videos — banned as overused: 'how is this even legal', '<rival> owners are sweating', 'means business', 'game-changer'. Each video needs its OWN fresh, specific, Indian-relatable humor (potholes, speed breakers, family weddings, the neighbour, EMIs).

Write for the SPOKEN voiceover: say 'driver-assist' not ADAS, 'four-wheel-drive' not 4XPLOR, 'low-range' not 4-Low, 'Newton-metres' not Nm. Short, easy-to-pronounce, easy-to-understand lines — no dense technical strings. Acronyms/short forms belong ONLY in on-screen pops (read, not spoken).
data_learnings: [high][data][retention-2026-08-05] THE SPEC BEAT IS THE #1 DROP-OFF. Across 7 videos, 55-81% of ALL departures happen DURING the spec beat (right after the hook) — the hook grips, then the spec deflates it. The cliff is the HOOK->SPEC seam, not spec->value. Fixes: (1) bridge the hook tension INTO the spec ("here is the crazy part…", "and it gets better") so the spec reads as the payoff, not a fact-dump; (2) keep the spec to ONE tight escalating line (the 123-word Thars bled 80-81%%; the 71-word Sonet bled least); (3) never open the spec with a flat number recital — lead with the surprise, explain after.

[medium][analyst] five_things: put numbered chips ①-⑤ on-screen synced to each item's phrase and persist an 'N/5' counter through the beat — CarWale + MotorOctane converge on this; our five_things renders lack the persistent counter that acts as a visible progress bar and lifts completion.

[medium][analyst] Comment-bait CTA on the tail card: append a binary poll (e.g. 'Nexon or Brezza — 1 or 2? comment') AFTER the verdict, keeping the approved LIKE·SHARE·SUBSCRIBE reaction — MotorOctane's engagement lever, harvests reply signal that recommender uses.

[medium][analyst] Hype hook overlay: first written word is an ALL-CAPS superlative verb (SHOCK / SHOULD / NEVER / ONLY / MUST) on frame 1 with a screen-punch stinger; MotorOctane's curiosity-gap stopping power — fits the hype persona five_things Nexon slot.

[medium][analyst] Authority anchor in first 1.5s: prefix hook with a 1-beat source chip ('CARDEKHO SPEC', 'SPEC SHEET', 'TEST DATA') — CarWale/carwow trust move; visibly separates our sourced-sheet facts from unverified reel noise and reduces the 3s cliff drop.

[high][mechanic] Payoff card (kind=card) now holds until section end -0.3 (was min-2.2s); rail pops fire AFTER the 2.2s count-up (only suppressed if they start inside the count-up window). Keeps the value figure on screen while the voice keeps talking about it AND lets concrete feature pops render below.

[high][mechanic] CTA narration containing 'like, share, subscribe' (any punctuation) auto-generates a graphic pop kind=lss — three PIL icons (thumbs-up, share arrow, bell) drawn procedurally, slam-in at y=0.30. NEVER write a text pop for those words; the engine draws the graphic. Scriptwright prompt now enforces the spoken phrase + which-car-next question in every CTA.

[high][mechanic] Empty rework verdict (notes+beat_tags+beat_wins all empty) MUST NOT invent changes and MUST NOT escalate to the paid deep brain — free brain now short-circuits: card flips back to awaiting_approval with a 'tag beats or leave a note' prompt. Ledger #1 (invented --no-kwcaps from ambiguous input) is the tax we already paid; do not pay it again.
[high][mechanic] Voice ceilings are PER-VOICE: NeerjaExpressive at +3% fits ~112 words in 62s; always re-check runtime after any voice or rate change — cached audio must never mask it.

[high][data] PROVEN WINNER (2026-07-31): the tight format is our biggest hit — Kia Sonet 30s, hero number in the hook, ONE spec beat, real owner footage, calm delivery = 1244 views (2.6x the prior best). Swift 46s loops at 130% retention (curve >100% end-to-end). FORMULA to replicate: <=35s, hero number in the hook, at most one proof beat, real footage, loop-friendly close. Cadence over polish.

[high][data] Distribution is ~95% SHORTS FEED (thumbnail impressions/CTR do not apply to Shorts). Retention + loops are the ONLY feed lever, and it is episodic (a video catches the feed or dies in a day). Engagement is the CEILING: 1 subscriber + 1 comment across 1700 views. Levers: ask for the LIKE at the dopamine peak (after the payoff), make the CTA a RIVALRY poll people argue about, and end loop-friendly so the last line feeds the hook.

[high][data][sierra-2026-08-03] FRAME 1 = MOTION, not a static card. Sierra's swipe-away was high (only ~23% stayed when it hit the feed). The hero number STAYS in the hook (proven winner), but the FIRST visible frame must be the car MOVING or a bold hero exterior — never a static badge/interior/price-card cold-open. A boring frame 1 loses the swipe before a single word is heard. The price belongs in the spoken line + an overlay punch, not as the opening image.

[high][data][sierra-2026-08-03] MID-POINT is the cliff. Sierra held ~48% (12s of 25s) with the drop at the spec->verdict handoff. Bridge that seam with a one-beat mini-cliffhanger BEFORE the value/peak ('but here's the catch', 'the best bit is the price') so the payoff beat reads as a reveal, not a topic switch. Never let 'specs' and 'the deal' feel like two separate videos stapled together.

[high][data][sierra-2026-08-03] TIGHT OUTRO. Sierra spent ~5-6s on the CTA tail; that dead air at the end drags average-view-% down and delays the loop. Keep the CTA <=4s: fast 'like, share, subscribe' + a <=8-word rivalry poll, then a loop-friendly last line that feeds the hook. A punchy 3s close beats a polite 6s one.

[high][data][sierra-2026-08-03] EVERY NAMED FEATURE gets a synced on-screen overlay at the exact word. Sierra narrated 'Dolby sound' with NO on-screen overlay (the sunroof got one, audio didn't) - the brain critic caught it, deterministic QA did not. If a beat names two features, it needs two pops. Naked feature mentions waste the muted-viewer's eyes and the retention beat.

[high][mechanic][overlays-2026-08-03] Overlays went PREMIUM: retired the heavy Montserrat-Black + tech-cyan + thick meme-stroke look. Two selectable themes, auto-alternated per render for an A/B test (produce --overlay-theme luxe|frost|auto; recorded in manifest render.overlay_theme). A 'luxe' = thin/light weight, wide letter-spacing, boxless, champagne accent (owner's pick). B 'frost' = semibold in a smoked-glass panel, champagne rule. Both: generous TRACKING (the amateur->pro tell), ONE metallic accent (champagne #DEC58C, never cyan/yellow), no heavy stroke. When comparing performance, read overlay_theme from each video's manifest and attribute retention to the look.

[high][mechanic][overlays-2026-08-03] Count-up card bugfix: a unit label ('₹11.49L · EX-SHOWROOM') must NEVER share the giant number line — it clips off both frame edges. The card now splits on '·' into a small tracked kicker + the big value, and hard-clamps the value width to the safe box. Keep card 'show' text as VALUE · LABEL and the engine handles the split.
